risks.risk: Exact fitment is unknown (vehicle make/model/engine type not readable), so the buyer may receive mounts that don’t bolt up.
risks.proof: Ask for a clear photo of any part numbers/markings and the vehicle/model it came from (e.g., engine code or chassis) plus a photo showing the mounting bolt-hole pattern close-up.
risks.if_unproven: Price as generic/unknown-fit used engine mounts (worst case: may not fit).

risks.risk: Condition is uncertain beyond visible rust (bushings may be torn, loose, or mounts may be bent).
risks.proof: Ask for close-up photos of each bushing/isolator and a short video showing the rubber/metal play (push/pull) and whether any mount is cracked or separated.
risks.if_unproven: Price as used mounts with possible wear/damage (worst case: not fully serviceable).

risks.risk: Quantity and which exact pieces are included is unclear (photo shows many parts; seller may be selling only some).
risks.proof: Ask for a numbered list of included pieces and a photo laid out with counts (e.g., '1x left mount, 1x right mount, 2x brackets...').
risks.if_unproven: Price as the lowest-value subset (worst case: fewer usable pieces than expected).

proof_requests: Confirm the exact quantity and list of included mounts/brackets (with a laid-out photo showing counts).
Provide close-up photos of each bushing/isolator (showing cracks/tears) and any part numbers/markings.
Tell the vehicle make/model/engine it came from and share a photo of the donor car/engine bay or fitment reference.
Send a short video testing for looseness/play in the bushings (push/pull) and checking for bent brackets.
response.reason: The photo shows engine/gearbox mounting parts, but the exact fitment, quantity, and serviceable condition cannot be confirmed from the single image; without that, a reliable worst-case price selection from the comparables isn’t possible.
